reason: An item renders an <a> when it has href and a <button> when it does not, so no single interactive pattern always applies to it. Binding `button` with a blanket exception would leave a reader of the binding alone believing the pattern always holds, which is the false half of an honest problem -- and that is why `none` plus this prose was chosen when it was written. The schema CAN now say "this pattern applies only when href is absent": a binding may declare `cases`, one per render configuration, and `Tag` -- which once carried exactly the blanket exception described above -- now declares `plain` -> `none` and `removable` -> `button`. SideNavItem is expressible the same way: a `button` case, and an <a href> case binding `none`, since there is no link pattern to bind. It was simply not converted -- it sat outside 8C9's scope -- so what stands here is an UNCONVERTED CASE rather than evidence of a limit, and converting it means writing a render suite covering both shapes. What genuinely remains unexpressible is a pattern conditional on CONSUMER usage rather than on a component's own props; that limit is recorded in CLAUDE.md's Known debt -- count the set there rather than trusting an ordinal written here, which goes stale the next time a batch adds one. What the element it does render carries -- a link's or a button's implicit role, its native keyboard, aria-current on the active one -- comes from the platform and from SideNav's own `navigation` binding, neither of which this binding weakens.
